null-hypothesis.def: The statement that the independent variable has no effect: any difference between groups is due to chance alone (H₀). It is the statement an experiment tests.

alternative-hypothesis.def: The statement that the independent variable does have an effect, so groups really differ (H₁ or Hₐ). It may name a direction ("higher temperature increases leakage") or not ("temperature changes leakage").

reject-null.def: The decision made from data: reject the null hypothesis when the difference between groups is too large to blame on chance, or fail to reject it when it is not. A null hypothesis is never "accepted" or "proved".
